prompt: Why didn't Harvard have calculus classes when it first opened?
answer:
Harvard didn’t offer calculus when it first opened because modern calculus had not yet been developed. Harvard began operating in 1636–1638, while Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz developed and published the foundations of calculus only in the late 17th century, roughly 30–50 years later.

Early Harvard’s curriculum therefore focused on classical subjects—Latin, Greek, theology, logic, arithmetic, and geometry—rather than derivatives, integrals, or limits. Calculus was introduced at Harvard later, during the 18th century, as the new mathematical ideas spread from Europe.
